sections.h2: What are the fastest ways to sell a house in West Palm Beach, FL?
sections.html:
The fastest routes are a direct sale to a cash buyer or investor, or a short agent listing priced to move. A West Palm Beach seller who needs certainty on timing usually weighs three things: price, days to close, and how much repair work the buyer will demand.

  • Cash or investor sale: the buyer buys as-is and the closing date is often your choice.
  • Agent listing: a wider buyer pool and often a higher price, with showings and lender timelines.
  • Hybrid: list first, then take a cash offer if the market response is slow.

Compare offers on what you net after the deed tax, title charges, any unpaid taxes and a rental license transfer if the house is a rental. A higher headline price can net less than a lower cash offer once those lines are added.

sections.h2: What is West Palm Beach and why does its housing mix matter to a seller?
sections.html:
West Palm Beach is the county seat of Palm Beach County, and the city's own history page says it was incorporated on November 5, 1894, two years before Miami. It reports roughly 1,000 residents in 1895 and an estimated population of 120,000 or more.

The same page lists the places buyers know: The Square, Clematis Street, Antique Row and Northwood Village, plus the Kravis Center, the Norton Museum of Art and the Grassy Waters Everglades Preserve on the western edge. It also notes that Palm Beach Junior College, Florida's first junior college, opened in 1933 and that thousands of servicemen passed through the city's airport in World War II.

That age shows in the housing stock. Historic neighborhoods sit alongside newer waterfront and downtown buildings. An older house may carry deferred maintenance, so an as-is sale can save a seller the cost of repairs before listing.

sections.h2: Does West Palm Beach require a rental license when a house is sold or leased?
sections.html:
Yes. The city's Rental Property Guidelines say all rental units must secure a rental tax application, whether the unit is a short-term listing on a platform like Airbnb or a lease to a tenant, and that processing generally takes seven to 10 business days.

Owners are also asked to complete a zoning review that verifies the number of units, and the page lists interior and exterior conditions inspectors look for, such as working appliances, window screens, paved parking and visible address numbers. After applying, the owner contacts Code Enforcement at (561) 822-1465.

Rental property types in West Palm Beach, as the city's guidelines define them
TypeDescriptionExtra requirement noted
Type 1Owner-occupied single-family, multifamily or duplexProof the property is owner-occupied; owner name must match the recorded deed
Type 2Not owner-occupied single-family or duplexEntire dwelling unit rented
Type 3Not owner-occupied multifamily, such as apartments or condosBuilding and unit counts; compliance with any geographic caps

If you sell a rental, tell the buyer which type applies. The page ties the ownership on the application to the deed recorded with the Palm Beach County Clerk's Office, so a new owner has to apply in their own name.

sections.h2: How do code enforcement and permits affect a West Palm Beach sale?
sections.html:
Open violations and unpermitted additions can slow a closing. Rental owners must hold a license and pass an inspection under the city's guidelines, so an extra unit added to a structure without paperwork is a likely sticking point.

The Rental Property Guidelines also say the code compliance division sets minimum standards for substandard housing conditions, trash and debris, yard upkeep and parking areas.

Before you list, walk the lot for visible issues, check that any garage conversion or added unit has paperwork, and ask Code Enforcement about open cases on the address. A buyer paying cash can take a property with problems, but the price will reflect the cleanup.

sections.h2: When are West Palm Beach property taxes due and what are the discounts?
sections.html:
Palm Beach County mails the bills, and the County Tax Collector says that by November 1 it sends more than 600,000 property tax bills, payable from November 1 through March 31. The Property Appraiser sends the proposed-tax notice each August.

  • November: 4 percent discount
  • December: 3 percent discount
  • January: 2 percent discount
  • February: 1 percent discount
  • March: no discount; April 1: taxes become delinquent

The tax collector's page adds that delinquent tax cannot be paid online and that postmark date is not proof of payment once a tax is delinquent. It also says a bill sent to a seller after a sale should be forwarded to the new owner, or the office can be told through a Property Sold Form. Questions about mailing address or exemptions go to the Property Appraiser at (561) 355-2866, and delinquent amounts to the Tax Collector at (561) 355-2264.

Your bill includes non-ad valorem charges as well as ad valorem tax. The county gives the Solid Waste Authority fee as an example, set by the type of property.

sections.h2: Can a West Palm Beach homeowner defer or limit property taxes?
sections.html:
Some owners can. Florida's Department of Revenue describes a homestead tax deferral filed on Form DR-570 with the tax collector by March 31, and installment prepayment applications due by May 1 of the assessment year.

Non-homestead property has its own protection: assessed value growth is limited to 10 percent each year. For homestead, the Save Our Homes cap holds yearly increases to the lower of 3 percent or the CPI change, and the cap resets when title changes. A buyer of your house may therefore see a higher assessment the following January 1 than you did.

A West Palm Beach seller who moves within Florida may carry some of that savings forward. Portability requires the new homestead to be established within three years of January 1 of the year the old homestead was abandoned, with Form DR-501T filed with the DR-501 by March 1.

sections.h2: What do deed and recording costs look like when selling in West Palm Beach?
sections.html:
The state deed tax is 70 cents per $100 of consideration, and Palm Beach County is not Miami-Dade, so the Miami-Dade rate does not apply. The Department of Revenue says all parties are liable, though the contract decides who pays.

The clerk's statutory recording charge is $5.00 for a first page and $4.00 for each additional page, with a $1.00 first-page and $0.50 additional-page trust fund charge and a $4 per page technology charge. Request a full settlement statement before you sign so each line is visible.

faqs.q: Can I sell a rental property in West Palm Beach without ending the rental license?
faqs.a: Plan on the buyer applying separately. The city's guidelines tie the application to the owner shown on the recorded deed, so a new owner should expect to file in their own name. Ask the Development Services business tax staff how to close out your account.

faqs.q: How long does the West Palm Beach rental license take?
faqs.a: The city says it is generally processed in seven to 10 business days. A zoning review of the unit count is part of the process.

faqs.q: When do West Palm Beach property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: April 1. Palm Beach County's tax collector says delinquent tax cannot be paid online and postmark date no longer counts as proof of payment.

faqs.q: Which discount applies if I pay in December?
faqs.a: A 3 percent discount applies for December payment, per the Palm Beach County Tax Collector. November is 4 percent, January 2 percent and February 1 percent.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for small repairs before selling?
faqs.a: Often yes. Florida's 2026 permit exemption for projects under $7,500 has limits, and electrical, plumbing and structural work still need permits. Ask the city's Development Services staff before starting work.
